title: The 10 Best Wire Crimping Tools
subtitle: Ratcheting and plier-style crimpers for insulated, non-insulated and heat-shrink terminals, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A crimper squeezes a terminal or butt connector onto stripped wire so it holds without solder. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Klein, Channellock, IRWIN, TITAN, haisstronica and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a ratchet that won't release until the crimp is complete, heat-shrink dies, interchangeable dies, a built-in cutter and color-coded cavities). Plier crimpers are cheap and double as cutters; ratcheting crimpers give the same crimp every time. They run from about $12 for IRWIN's 2078310 to $50 for haisstronica's six-die set.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Klein Tools 3005CR Wire Crimper Tool for Insulated Terminals
products.verdict: Klein's ratcheting crimper for red, blue and yellow insulated terminals. The ratchet holds until the crimp cycle is complete, and the compound action adds force to each squeeze.
products.best_for: Electricians and installers crimping lots of standard insulated terminals.
products.skip_if: You use heat-shrink connectors; Klein says it crimps insulated terminals only.

products.name: haisstronica Crimping Tool for Heat Shrink Connectors, AWG 26-10, HS-8327
products.verdict: A ratcheting crimper with jaws shaped for heat-shrink butt connectors, from 26 up to 10 AWG, with a quick-release lever inside the handle.
products.best_for: Boat, car and trailer wiring with heat-shrink connectors.
products.skip_if: You mostly crimp nylon insulated terminals; a die made for those fits better.

products.name: Klein Tools 1005 Cutting/Crimping Tool, Made in USA, Cutter/Crimper for 10-22 AWG Insulated and Non-Insulated Terminals

specs.extras: Hardened cutter in the nose; made in USA

products.verdict: A made-in-USA plier crimper with marked dies for insulated and non-insulated terminals, a hardened wire cutter in the nose and a tapered tip for tight boxes.
products.best_for: Electricians who want one slim tool that crimps and cuts.
products.skip_if: You want identical crimps every time; a ratcheting tool takes the guesswork out.
cons: Crimp quality depends on your grip

products.name: Channellock 909 9.5-Inch Wire Crimping Tool, Terminal Crimp Pliers with Cutter for Insulated and Non-Insulated Connections
products.verdict: Channellock's 9.5-inch crimper puts the cutter in the middle of the jaw for more leverage, with laser heat-treated cutting edges and forged high carbon steel.
products.best_for: Anyone who cuts heavy wire as often as they crimp.
products.skip_if: You want a ratchet; this is a plain plier crimper.

products.name: TITAN 11477 Ratcheting Wire Terminal Crimper Tool for Insulated Terminals, Fixed Jaw Crimper

specs.extras: Double crimp die, adjustable force, quick release

products.verdict: A ratcheting double-crimp tool for nylon insulated terminals with adjustable force and a quick-release lever. TITAN says not to use it on heat-shrink connectors.
products.best_for: DIYers who want a ratcheting crimper for insulated terminals at about $20.

products.name: Plustool Crimping Tool for Heat Shrink Connectors AWG26-10, Ratcheting Wire Terminal Crimper
products.verdict: A low-cost ratcheting crimper for heat-shrink connectors, with a star wheel that adjusts crimp height and cushioned handles.
products.best_for: Car and appliance repairs with heat-shrink butt connectors on a budget.
products.skip_if: You need a model number to trace; the listing doesn't give one.

products.name: Klein Tools 80013 Wire Stripper/Ratcheting Crimper Kit with Automatic Wire Stripper and Insulated Terminal Crimper, 2-Piece
products.verdict: The Klein 3005CR ratcheting crimper paired with Klein's automatic wire stripper and cutter, so one purchase covers stripping, cutting and crimping.
products.best_for: Setting up a wiring kit from scratch with name-brand tools.
products.skip_if: You already own a good stripper; the 3005CR alone costs less.
pros: Crimper and stripper in one kit
cons: About $13 more than the crimper alone

products.name: haisstronica 6PCS Crimping Tool Set, Interchangeable Terminal Dies

specs.terminals: 6 dies incl. heat shrink and insulated

products.verdict: One ratcheting handle with six AWG-marked dies that swap in for heat-shrink, insulated and other terminal types.
products.best_for: Hobbyists and mechanics who crimp many connector types.
products.skip_if: You only crimp one kind of terminal; a single-purpose crimper costs half as much.

products.name: WORKPRO 9.5" Wire Cutter/Crimper, Cr-V Steel Wire Crimping/Cutting Tool
products.verdict: A 9.5-inch plier crimper and cutter in 63-65 HRC steel, with gripping jaws for pulling and bending wire and a tapered nose.
products.best_for: A cheap all-round crimp-and-cut plier for the toolbox.
products.skip_if: You want a name you can find parts or support for; Klein and Channellock cost a little more.

products.name: IRWIN 2078310 Vise-Grip Forged Wire Crimper with ProTouch Grips, 10-Inch
products.verdict: IRWIN's forged 10-inch Vise-Grip crimper for 10-22 AWG terminals, with a wire cutter and cushioned grips. The cheapest name-brand crimper here.
products.best_for: Occasional crimping on a tight budget.
products.skip_if: You crimp every day; a ratcheting tool is easier on the hand.

avoid.name: Wire Crimping tool Wire crimper, stripper and cutter for Insulated/Bare/Heat Shrink Connectors (22-10 AWG)
avoid.flag: Plier sold as a heat-shrink crimper; specs contradict
avoid.verdict: An $8 plier sold as a heat-shrink crimper, with a listing whose own details disagree with each other.
reasons: The title claims heat-shrink connectors, but it is a plain plier with no ratchet. Heat-shrink butt connectors need a ratcheting die to crimp without splitting the sleeve, which is why the Plustool and haisstronica tools exist.
The material field says carbon steel while the bullets say CR-V steel, and the model number field is a random ID string.
The IRWIN 2078310 costs a few dollars more, is forged, and is honest about what it crimps.

buyers_guide.a: A plier crimper is cheap, slim and usually has a cutter, but how hard you squeeze decides the crimp. A ratcheting crimper won't open until it has completed the full stroke, so every crimp gets the same force. If you crimp more than a few terminals a year, the ratchet is worth it.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a special crimper for heat-shrink connectors?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. Heat-shrink butt connectors have a thin sleeve that standard insulated-terminal dies can split. Use a crimper made for heat-shrink connectors, like the Plustool, the haisstronica HS-8327 or the heat-shrink die in a set. TITAN and Klein both say their insulated-terminal crimpers are not for heat shrink.

buyers_guide.q: What do the red, blue and yellow colors mean?
buyers_guide.a: They are the standard insulated terminal sizes: red for 22-16 AWG, blue for 16-14 AWG, yellow for 12-10 AWG. Color-coded cavities on the crimper match the terminal's color, so you can't pick the wrong die.

buyers_guide.q: Can these crimp battery cable lugs?
buyers_guide.a: No. Everything here tops out at 10 AWG. Battery and welding cable lugs (8 AWG up to 4/0) need a hammer crimper or a hydraulic crimper.

buyers_guide.q: Do I still need a wire stripper?
buyers_guide.a: Usually. Plier crimpers often strip small wire badly or not at all. The Klein 80013 kit includes an automatic stripper; otherwise see our wire strippers page.
